RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

An all-male panel is, on its own, weak evidence. In structural engineering it's close to the demographic baseline — it's as consistent with who holds senior roles as with bias. It matters mainly as context, not as your argument.

Your stronger facts are substantive: nearly double the experience, equivalent licence, three major projects led, beaten by a candidate whose stated edge is the vaguest criterion on the list ("client relationships" — the classic place unexamined preference hides). And two weeks of silence on a reasonable written request is itself a problem.

So press for the written reasons and the scoring against stated criteria. Mention panel composition as one factor if you escalate, never as the headline.
